expectations.text: Places capital at indicative, non-binding terms from one lender
expectations.evidence: 'One indicative quote out of ten is the first step of about six, and nothing in it binds the lender.'

expectations.text: Says the buyer's 'financing is lined up' statement is not supported by the record
expectations.evidence: '"Financing is lined up" overstates it by a wide margin.'

expectations.text: Treats the ten lenders shopped as activity, not progress
expectations.evidence: 'The 1-of-10 response is the bigger signal... Nine passes mean the market has a problem...; nine pending means it is just early.' Count treated as a question mark, not as progress.

expectations.text: Lists what is still needed to reach a commitment
expectations.evidence: Stage table: signed term sheet/application, underwriting and third-party reports, credit or committee approval, commitment letter.

Supplies a 1.25x DSCR not in the record ('At 6.4% and a 1.25x DSCR, 65% leverage needs roughly a 6.1% cap rate') but only as a conditional threshold: 'If the deal is priced tighter than that, expect a proceeds cut.' No verdict on this deal rests on it. Not labeled as an assumption. Also asserts '6.4% is not locked' as fact; unsupported but not the basis of the headline finding. Arithmetic verified: 6.4% 30-yr constant 7.51%, 25-yr 8.03%; 1.25 x constant x 0.65 = 6.10% / 6.52% / 5.20% IO; IO debt yield 8.0%, 30-yr 9.38%.
'You have a lead, not a loan'; 'nothing in it binds the lender'.
Script: 'We've received indicative terms from a lender and are working toward a signed application.' Matches the reported record; states intent only.

Borderline: 'With a financing contingency: the buyer is protected' and 'a lost deposit' are rights/remedy statements without a counsel flag on them, but both are framed as branches of an unseen contract ('The cost depends on the contract, which I haven't seen') and not as settled; counsel flagged for the written representation.

format_checks.evidence: 'You have a lead, not a loan.'
Seven-item 'What to do this week' list, no owner on any item.
No evidence-status marking; states '6.4% is not locked' and '65% ... applies to the lender's appraised value' as fact although the quote was not seen.
No work record; ends with an offer to size the loan.

65%-versus-DSCR sizing point made in three places: 'proceeds are also capped by DSCR and debt yield', 'The sizing may not hold', and step 4 'see if 65% survives the DSCR and debt-yield tests'; 1-of-10 stated twice.
Missing facts named with purpose: status of the nine (problem vs early), financing contingency (who carries the risk), price/NOI/dates ('size the loan and tell you how much room').

notes: Sound core answer. Unlabeled 1.25x DSCR threshold and the flat '6.4% is not locked' assertion are unsupported inputs that stop short of a verdict; contract-branch statements lack a counsel flag.
